question: How do published message-passing topological neural networks (over hypergraphs, simplicial, cellular and combinatorial complexes) compare under one unified notation?
contributions: A pedagogical resource accessible to newcomers interested in applying TNNs to real-world problems.
A comprehensive and critical review of TNNs, their implementations and practical applications, with equations rewritten in our notation available at https://github.com/awesome-tnns.
A summary of open research questions, challenges, and opportunities for innovation.

limits: Survey only: no experiments, no benchmark numbers; Table I lists only comparison level (Graph, GNN SOTA, TNN SOTA), not scores.
Covers message-passing TNNs only; topological data analysis (persistent homology) approaches are out of scope.
Combinatorial complexes: authors say a more extensive analysis is needed to quantify the advantages of this domain; only HOAN implemented, without shared code.
Equations are written in spatial form only; spectral form not covered.
Literature stops at early 2023; the TDL field has moved since.
practices: Choose the domain by data: SC for triangular-mesh geometry, CC when part-whole interactions involve more than three nodes (e.g. benzene rings), HG for arbitrary-size equal-importance interactions (citation networks, protein complexes), CCC for nested molecular hierarchy (Sec II-A).
Avoid SC lifting when the data lack the strict geometric constraints; it adds spurious connections (Sec II-A2).
Use aggregation functions that are permutation invariant, such as mean or sum, on hypergraphs (Sec III-C).
Keep hypergraph structure during learning rather than clique-expanding to a graph (Sec III-A1).
Describe any TNN layer by its four message passing steps: message, within-neighborhood aggregation, between-neighborhood aggregation, update (Sec II-C1).

size n_{r-1} x n_r, entry +/-1 when the (r-1)-cell is on the boundary of the r-cell, else 0; sign is always +1 for HGs and CCCs
boundary, co-boundary, lower adjacent, upper adjacent
H_r = L_down,r + L_up,r; L_down,r = B_r B_r^T and L_up,r = B_{r+1}^T B_{r+1}
static domain is identical for each layer; dynamic changes from layer to layer
homogeneous uses the same feature dimension d for all ranks; heterogeneous has dimension depending on rank
hypergraph message passing with information flowing from nodes to hyperedges then back to nodes
